title: Transpapillary Placement of a Multihole Covered Metal Stent Using a 5.9-Fr Delivery System Through a Forward-viewing Endoscope in Malignant Biliary Obstruction With Type I Duodenal Stenosis

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Transpapillary Placement of a Multihole Covered Metal Stent Using a 5.9-Fr Delivery System Through a Forward-viewing Endoscope in Malignant Biliary Obstruction With Type I Duodenal Stenosis》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · deo270392-sec-0010-p1】Concurrent malignant biliary obstruction (MBO) and duodenal stenosis are common in advanced pancreatobiliary cancers [1, 2]. When duodenal stenosis occurs proximal to the major duodenal papilla (type I), advancing a standard side‐viewing duodenoscope is often technically unfeasible, making conventional transpapillary biliary drainage challenging [2, 3].

【Introduction · deo270392-sec-0010-p2】Although endoscopic ultrasound‐guided biliary drainage (EUS‐BD) and percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage (PTBD) are established alternatives, they require specific expertise and carry risks such as bile leakage and related complications [2, 4].

evidence.text: Concurrent malignant biliary obstruction (MBO) and duodenal stenosis are common in advanced pancreatobiliary cancers [1, 2]. When duodenal stenosis occurs proximal to the major duodenal papilla (type I), advancing a standard side‐viewing duodenoscope is often technically unfeasible, making conventional transpapillary biliary drainage challenging [2, 3].

Although endoscopic ultrasound‐guided biliary drainage (EUS‐BD) and percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage (PTBD) are established alternatives, they require specific expertise and carry risks such as bile leakage and related complications [2, 4].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:

【Introduction · deo270392-sec-0010-p4】Recently, a novel covered multihole SEMS with an ultra‐slim 5.9‐Fr delivery system has become available. Herein, we report successful transpapillary placement of a covered multihole SEMS using this 5.9‐Fr delivery system through a standard FVE in a patient with MBO complicated by type I duodenal stenosis, and discuss the clinical utility of this approach in the context of the current literature.

【Case Report · deo270392-sec-0020-p1】A 66‐year‐old woman was found to have a 35‐mm mass in the head of the pancreas in February 2025. EUS‐guided fine‐needle aspiration (EUS‐FNA) confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. Gadolinium ethoxybenzyl diethylenetriamine pentaacetic acid–enhanced magnetic resonance imaging revealed small liver metastases, and she was diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer. The patient received eight courses of gemcitabine plus nab‐paclitaxel.

【Case Report · deo270392-sec-0020-p1】A 66‐year‐old woman was found to have a 35‐mm mass in the head of the pancreas in February 2025. EUS‐guided fine‐needle aspiration (EUS‐FNA) confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. Gadolinium ethoxybenzyl diethylenetriamine pentaacetic acid–enhanced magnetic resonance imaging revealed small liver metastases, and she was diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer. The patient received eight courses of gemcitabine plus nab‐paclitaxel.

【Case Report · deo270392-sec-0020-p4】On day 16, the cholangitis recurred. Repeat ERCP using a side‐viewing duodenoscope was considered; however, the progression of tumor‐related duodenal stenosis precluded the passage of the JF‐260 V. In contrast, a FVE (GIF‐Q260J; Olympus Medical Systems) was used to traverse the stenosis. Biliary cannulation was achieved under direct visualization using a Zemex articulating cannula (Zeon Medical Inc., Tokyo, Japan). After the removal of the biliary plastic stents, a 6‐Fr ENBD tube (Flexima; Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA, USA) was inserted. The patient remained able to tolerate oral intake; therefore, duodenal intervention was not considered necessary at that time.

evidence.text: A 66‐year‐old woman was found to have a 35‐mm mass in the head of the pancreas in February 2025. EUS‐guided fine‐needle aspiration (EUS‐FNA) confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. Gadolinium ethoxybenzyl diethylenetriamine pentaacetic acid–enhanced magnetic resonance imaging revealed small liver metastases, and she was diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer. The patient received eight courses of gemcitabine plus nab‐paclitaxel.

On day 16, the cholangitis recurred. Repeat ERCP using a side‐viewing duodenoscope was considered; however, the progression of tumor‐related duodenal stenosis precluded the passage of the JF‐260 V. In contrast, a FVE (GIF‐Q260J; Olympus Medical Systems) was used to traverse the stenosis. Biliary cannulation was achieved under direct visualization using a Zemex articulating cannula (Zeon Medical Inc., Tokyo, Japan). After the removal of the biliary plastic stents, a 6‐Fr ENBD tube (Flexima; Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA, USA) was inserted. The patient remained able to tolerate oral intake; therefore, duodenal intervention was not considered necessary at that time.

【FIGURE 1 · deo270392-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 Contrast‐enhanced computed tomography (CE‐CT) at admission. CE‐CT shows a pancreatic head mass causing distal biliary obstruction with upstream bile duct dilatation and concomitant duodenal stenosis due to tumor invasion.

【FIGURE 2 · deo270392-fig-0002】FIGURE 2 Endoscopic images of the transpapillary biliary stenting procedure. (A) Endoscopic view of the major duodenal papilla obtained using a standard forward‐viewing endoscope after traversing the type I duodenal stenosis. Biliary cannulation is performed with an articulating cannula. (B) Insertion of the ultra‐slim 5.9‐Fr delivery system into the bile duct under direct endoscopic visualization. (C) Final endoscopic view showing the successfully placed covered multihole self‐expandable metal stent (SEMS) at the papilla.

【FIGURE 3 · deo270392-fig-0003】FIGURE 3 Fluoroscopic images showing transpapillary biliary stenting via a standard forward‐viewing endoscope. (A) Biliary cannulation achieved using an articulating cannula and a 0.025‐inch guidewire through a standard forward‐viewing endoscope (GIF‐Q260J). (B) Advancement of the ultra‐slim 5.9‐Fr delivery system through the 3.2‐mm working channel of the endoscope. (C) Successful deployment of a 6 mm × 60 mm covered multihole self‐expandable metal stent (SEMS) across the distal biliary stricture.
